notes: Accessibility cases for the consolidated visual-patterns.md → Accessibility section (#39), checked against tagged upstream sources on 2026-10-12: huh v2.0.3 accessible mode (form.go, field sources), Bubble Tea v2.1.0 and Bubbles v2.2.1 (no screen-reader support), gh's accessible prompter and spinner settings (cli/cli trunk, GitHub changelog 2025-05-01), Ink 8.0.0 screen-reader rendering (renderer.ts, render-node-to-output.ts, Box.tsx), Gemini CLI v0.63.0 and Claude Code accessibility docs, Textual 8.2.8 (roadmap, animation levels) and textual-serve 1.1.3's xterm.js client, ratatui#2610, the NVDA 2026.2 user guide, Windows Terminal's 2023 accessibility notes, and Sampath, Merrick, and Macvean, CHI '21 (doi:10.1145/3411764.3445544). Assertions define the grading rubric; improvement claims require a recorded harness run against one immutable skill hash.

evals.name: bubbletea-form-screen-reader
evals.prompt: Blind users of our Go CLI say the onboarding form is unusable with NVDA. It's a Huh v2 form running full-screen inside our Bubble Tea v2 app. How do we make it work for them?
assertions: Recommends Huh's accessible mode (WithAccessible(true)), which asks each field as a plain line-by-line prompt instead of a full-screen redraw
Puts the mode behind a switch the user controls (flag, environment variable, or persistent setting) rather than relying on screen-reader detection
Explains that the full-screen form's repaints (moving the highlight, redrawing the frame) are re-read by the screen reader, which is why linear prompts work better
States that Bubble Tea itself has no screen-reader support, so the app's other screens need their own linear output
Keeps every answer settable through flags or config so the form can be skipped entirely

evals.name: no-tui-output-contract
evals.prompt: Our Ratatui dashboard has a --no-tui flag that currently prints the same table without borders and exits. A screen-reader user says it doesn't help. What should --no-tui actually do and output?
assertions: Makes every action available in the TUI reachable in plain mode, not just a read-only dump of one view
Replaces aligned columns with labelled lines (Header: value) or offers a structured format such as CSV or JSON
Keeps results on stdout and prompts, progress, and diagnostics on stderr
Reports status and progress as words (a final status line, occasional progress lines), with no spinner frames or redrawn bars
Removes reliance on color, column position, or box drawing to carry meaning
Lets the user enable the mode persistently (environment variable or config), not only per invocation

evals.name: textual-serve-accessibility
evals.prompt: Is running our Textual app with `textual serve` a good way to make it accessible to screen-reader users, since browsers have good screen-reader support?
assertions: Says no: textual serve paints the terminal grid in a browser terminal (xterm.js on a canvas) with screen-reader support off, so screen readers gain nothing
States that Textual has no screen-reader support of its own
Recommends a linear, plain-text mode or CLI path for screen-reader users instead

evals.name: ink-screen-reader-live-region
evals.prompt: We added INK_SCREEN_READER=true support to our Ink 8 chat app, but NVDA users say it keeps re-reading the conversation and the spinner. Why, and what should we change?
assertions: Explains that Ink's screen-reader mode linearizes output but still erases and rewrites the whole live (non-Static) region on every change
Moves finished messages into <Static> so they are written once, and keeps the live region small
Stops per-tick updates such as spinners and timers in screen-reader mode, replacing them with a static status line
Uses aria-label or aria-hidden for visual-only elements
Exposes the mode through the app's own flag or setting, since Ink never detects a screen reader
